pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are 0 and 2 is rejected.
src/index.js WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id; 'AC-2' test covers / and ?view=open with one item marked done.
'AC-3' test: done view returns only done items in id order (3 and 1 marked), prefixed ✓.
'AC-4' test checks all three in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' test: Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values all give 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
'AC-7' test covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json lists both views; the 'AC-8' test checks them. The traffic worker passes route strings straight into the request URL, and the checker's regex now allows a query.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its two decisions: it opens on open items and uses a query parameter. Nothing extra was added beyond the traffic-checker regex change the routes need.
All 8 acceptance items are met, and each has a test that names it. All 6 state-table rows have tests.
Tests assert rendered output and status codes, and would fail against broken code. I did not run them here; CI runs them per scripts/check-fast.sh.
The README describes the new views.
The view is validated with Object.hasOwn, and the SQL fragments come only from the constant VIEWS table. The count query for an empty table is correct.
The view value is allow-listed and never put into SQL. Titles are still HTML-escaped. No instructions planted in the repository.
The page is HTML but has only a minimal nav, with no stylesheet or design files. The nav markup is covered by the AC-5 test.
No browser flow was available. Rendered HTML is checked by tests.
The PR claims match the diff: the behaviour change, the traffic checker, the fake app change, and no deleted tests.
